title: Choose the look for the Ghost Diary
question: The roll assigned The Night Desk Handover. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Night Desk Handover
options.lineage: hotel night-porter handover sheets and the key-and-pigeonhole board behind the front desk
options.thesis: The ghosts are the hotel's night staff; the diary is the handover sheet the morning shift reads at 7 AM, under the key board where every issue hangs as a numbered tag.
options.viewport: Top: a dark-green key-board rail with one brass tag per issue, its hook state showing the outcome at a glance (key returned = PR opened, card on hook = needs you). Below: the handover card, a calm ivory reading column with a letterhead (date, repo, shift 01:00 to 01:47), the night totals, then timestamped entries in each ghost's voice. Each entry pairs the note with its evidence: PR link, diff count, test result.
options.risk: Ivory card plus a serif letterhead can slide toward the generic cream-and-serif look; the green rail and brass tags must carry the identity.

raised.raise: Every ghost's claim sits directly beside its proof (PR link, +/- lines, test count), never a note without evidence.
Outcome is a mark in a fixed column (filled, hollow, struck), not only a colour, so it survives greyscale and colour blindness.
The key rail shows the night's structure: one tag per issue, so the count of what shipped versus what needs you is visible before reading.

options.label: The Cobbler's Claim Tickets
options.lineage: shoe-repair claim stubs: numbered kraft tickets, string, a 'ready for pickup' stamp
options.thesis: The elves and the shoemaker, literally: each issue is a repair ticket, stamped READY overnight.
options.viewport: A rack of numbered kraft tickets across the top, each stamped with its outcome, above a reading column of the night's notes.
options.risk: It is the literal reading of the product's own metaphor, the first place most runs would go, and kraft-and-stamp leans craft-market.

options.label: Monochrome Product Canon
options.case: Fuses poorly: a morning report is not a marketing page, and it drops the Kiroween theme judges score.
options.kept: Every claim paired with its proof.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.case: Fuses poorly: raked containers and one type size slow the five-second morning glance.
options.kept: State as a mark in a fixed cell.

options.label: Cracktro Scroller
options.case: Fuses poorly: night-time mood is right, but reading diffs and notes in bitmap type on drifting dust fails clarity.
options.kept: One signal colour used only where action is needed.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.case: Fuses poorly: developers don't recognise an editing bench, and orange over a third of the screen fights the report.
options.kept: A flag marks exactly where your attention is needed.

options.label: Exposed Coptic Binding
options.case: Fuses poorly: lovely, but nothing about a night shift.
options.kept: Structure showing: the count of sections is visible.

options.label: Curved Crease Shell
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to developers, ghosts, or mornings.
options.kept: One governing line organises the page.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean dark developer report like GitHub or Linear, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Summary stats, then a list of issue rows with status pills and PR links.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every dashboard; little Kiroween theme for judges.
